clue.text: Face involving awkward bloke about numbers

indicators.note: involving means the clock face wraps round the awkward bloke

parts.note: a dial is the face of a clock or watch
a git is British slang for an annoying, awkward man

explanation.surface: Someone's face screws up around a difficult man who is talking about numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: GIT is mild British slang for an unpleasant or awkward person.
explanation.definitionFit: Digital describes data represented as figures, so it concerns numbers.

clue.text: Satisfied to receive six — final bonus

indicators.note: to receive means the satisfied word takes the number inside it

parts.note: did, as in 'that did me', means satisfied or sufficed
VI is six in Roman numerals
the end is the final part

explanation.surface: Happy to collect six, as a last reward.
explanation.definitionFit: A dividend is a share of profits paid out, an extra payment like a bonus.

clue.text: Guy heartlessly got up, about to get spinning toy

indicators.note: heartlessly means the middle letter of the name is removed
about means the got-up word goes round the get word

parts.note: rose means got up
cop is slang for get or catch

explanation.surface: A man rose too soon and went to fetch a spinning top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' drops the U from GUY; ROSE is wrapped about COP.
explanation.definitionFit: A gyroscope is a wheel spinning on an axis, often sold as a toy.

clue.text: Catch lines being raised

indicators.note: being raised in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an actor's part is their lines

explanation.surface: A fishing catch as lines are hauled up.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap is a device for catching animals, or a ruse that catches people out.

clue.text: Sporty head girl absorbing fashion and excitement in Bedfordshire town

indicators.note: absorbing means the reworked letters take in the other pieces
sporty suggests the letters jump about lively

parts.note: ton is an old word for fashion
a buzz is a thrill or excitement

explanation.surface: An athletic head girl taking in fashion and thrills in a small English town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sporty' rearranges HEAD GIRL into LEIGHARD, which 'absorbing' splits after LEIGH. Leighton Buzzard is a market town in Bedfordshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Leighton Buzzard is a real market town in the English county of Bedfordshire.

clue.text: European country backed hanging on to dismiss no-good Middle Easterner

indicators.note: backed means the two letters for the European country are read from right to left

parts.note: UK is the United Kingdom

indicators.note: to dismiss says the letters for no-good are sent away from the hanging-on word

parts.note: waiting is hanging on
NG is a standard abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: A European country retreats, clinging on while sacking a useless Middle Eastern man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns UK into KU; 'to dismiss' drops the N and G from WAITING, leaving WAITI.
explanation.definitionFit: A Kuwaiti is a native of Kuwait, a Gulf state in the Middle East.

clue.text: Campaign no longer motivating refuseniks?

parts.note: refuseniks read as people who drop refuse, rubbish, and the slogan no longer persuades litter louts

explanation.surface: A campaign that has stopped inspiring dissidents.
explanation.walkthrough: A refusenik is a protester, but here it is played as someone who leaves refuse about. Keep Britain Tidy is the long-running British anti-litter campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: The British anti-litter charity's slogan urges people not to drop rubbish.

clue.text: Leak here may take a moment or two

definitions.text: Leak here may take a moment or two

parts.words: Leak here may take a moment or two
parts.note: the steady dripping out of liquid is how this device counts passing time

explanation.surface: A plumber warns that repairing a leak will take a little time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' reads as measure: water leaking at a steady rate marks the moments.
explanation.definitionFit: A clepsydra, an ancient timer, measured hours by water flowing out of a vessel.

clue.text: I'd turned up in middle of nominated country

indicators.note: in means the upturned letters go inside the central letters
middle of says take the central three letters of nominated
turned up in a down clue means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: the letters of I'd without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone turned up amid a nominated country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' suits a down clue, where reversed letters read upwards; 'middle of' takes the central three letters of the nine.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a large nation of South Asia.

clue.text: Demonstrate airbrushing Italian restaurant — that's poor treatment

indicators.note: airbrushing means removing something from a picture, so these letters are taken out

parts.note: to illustrate is to demonstrate
trat is short for trattoria, an Italian restaurant

explanation.surface: Showing a doctored photo of an Italian restaurant amounts to unfair treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'airbrushing' strips TRAT from ILLUSTRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-use, as a noun, is cruel or unfair handling of someone.

clue.text: Engaging in various ways at one line in poetry

indicators.note: in means the first pieces are placed inside the word for poetry

parts.note: verse is poetry
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A description of someone engaging in different ways, each at one line of a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone versatile can turn their hand to many activities, adapting to each.

clue.text: Describing main variations, I'd article in The Listener at first

indicators.note: in means the pieces before it go inside the opening letters that follow
at first says take the opening letter of each of the two words before it

parts.note: the letters of I'd without the apostrophe
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A radio listener's magazine article about changes in the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The main is the open sea, so its variations are the rise and fall of tides. The Listener was a BBC weekly magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidal describes the regular rise and fall of the sea, the crossword's main.

clue.text: Occupant of farmyard is craving release

indicators.note: Occupant of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A farmyard animal is longing to be set free.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle farmyarD IS Craving.
explanation.definitionFit: A record company issues a disc as a new release of music.

clue.text: Asian highway of fundamental relevance to some Londoners?

definitions.meaning: the mountain route linking Afghanistan and Pakistan

definitions.text: of fundamental relevance to some Londoners?
definitions.meaning: in Cockney rhyming slang the phrase stands for arse, the fundamental or bottom

explanation.surface: A road in Asia that oddly matters to people in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang, from East London, replaces a word with a rhyming phrase: Khyber Pass rhymes with arse. 'Fundamental' is a jokey word for the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous pass is the historic road through the mountains between Afghanistan and Pakistan.

clue.text: Small number keeping mostly fixed diet

indicators.note: keeping means the outer pieces hold the trimmed word inside them

parts.note: low means small, as in a low figure

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: set means fixed
eight is a number

explanation.surface: A small number keeping largely to a fixed eating plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diet' looks like a noun but is the verb: to cut down on food.
explanation.definitionFit: To diet, as a verb, is to cut down food in order to shed pounds.

clue.text: Some local minion wantonly wasting one million in aggressive foreign policy

indicators.note: wantonly means the letters are thrown about without restraint
wasting says the letter for one million is lost from the mix

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for a million

explanation.surface: A petty official squandering a fortune in a bullying overseas policy.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange SOME LOCAL MINION after taking out one M ('wasting one million').
explanation.definitionFit: Neocolonialism is the use of economic or political pressure to control weaker countries abroad.

clue.text: Glancing attack? The team's clear

parts.note: a side is a team, plus the possessive s
to wipe is to clear

explanation.surface: A sports team clears a ball after a glancing tackle.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals the playful definition: a sideswipe literally glances off the side, and figuratively is an incidental criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideswipe is a blow struck in passing, or an offhand jibe.

clue.text: Gone dry, wrinkled, under hot gas

indicators.note: under in a down clue puts the reworked letters below the hot letter

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: wrinkled means the letters are crumpled into a new order

explanation.surface: Something has gone dry and wrinkled after lying under heat.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydrogen is the lightest chemical element, a colourless gas.

clue.text: Derby cameramen ruined commemorative event

indicators.note: ruined means the letters of the two words are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Photographers at the Derby horse race spoil a memorial occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is a famous English horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: Remembrance Day honours the war dead each November, an occasion of commemoration.

clue.text: Counter attack's beginning — support us after King decamps

indicators.note: beginning says take the first letter of attack
decamps means the king's letter leaves the support word

parts.note: to back is to support
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A counter-attack starts, with backing for us after the king flees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter' looks like part of 'counter-attack'; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a frame of beads used for counting, a counting device.

clue.text: Neutral area in the image of an old gentleman's club?

definitions.meaning: a strip of land separating hostile parties

definitions.text: the image of an old gentleman's club?
definitions.meaning: an old buffer is an elderly man, and a club full of them would be his territory

explanation.surface: A neutral room resembling an old gentlemen's club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buffer' is British slang for a fusty old man, so a zone of buffers is where such men gather.
explanation.definitionFit: A buffer zone is territory kept between opposing sides to stop them clashing.

clue.text: Signal line in foodstuffs

indicators.note: in means the line letter goes inside the food word

parts.note: fare is food

explanation.surface: A signal line running through food supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: A flare is a bright light fired as a distress signal.

clue.text: One employs a cat, say, but not second

indicators.note: but not says the letters for second are left out of the cat word

parts.note: a mouser is a cat, as an example of an animal that catches mice
mo is short for moment, a second

explanation.surface: Someone who employs a cat, though not a second one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One employs' is read as 'one who employs'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who employs something makes use of it, so is its operator.

clue.text: I'm surprised to enter university in part of Hawaii

indicators.note: to enter means the exclamation goes inside the university letters

parts.note: OU is the Open University
ah is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone expresses surprise at getting into a university in Hawaii.
explanation.walkthrough: The Open University is Britain's distance-learning university.
explanation.definitionFit: Oahu is one of the main islands of the Hawaiian group.

clue.text: Scottish family finally enjoying the clash of claymores?

parts.note: a clan is a Scottish family group

indicators.note: finally says take the closing letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: A Highland clan at last relishing a battle with broadswords.
explanation.walkthrough: A claymore is a large Scottish two-handed sword; the question mark admits the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal blades striking together make a loud ringing clang.

clue.text: An Independent magazine bringing in money — exciting

indicators.note: bringing in means the magazine word takes the money word inside it

parts.note: tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: The Independent's magazine earns cash, which is thrilling.
explanation.definitionFit: Animating means bringing to life, and so stirring up or exciting.

clue.text: One-third of scouts under canvas, not initially giving off a smell

indicators.note: one-third of says take the first two of the six letters of scouts
not initially says the first letter is dropped

parts.note: tented describes being in tents, under canvas

explanation.surface: A third of the scouts camping are starting to smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One-third of' takes SC from the six letters of SCOUTS; 'not initially' strips T from TENTED, leaving ENTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scented has a perfume and so gives off an odour.

clue.text: Our energy should be put into that? Agreed!

indicators.note: should be put into means the first pieces are placed inside the word for that

parts.note: yon is an old word for that, as in yon hill
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to invest their energy in that, and the other agrees.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase accepts a challenge or bet, a spoken way of saying it is agreed.
